newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INTERVIEW-Fine-tuning for The Warehouse.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Fine-tuning for The Warehouse.

text.p: The Warehouse Group Ltd managing director Stephen Tindall said on Friday the discount chain would further fine-tune its operations before considering new growth prospects.
Tindall told Reuters in an interview that the days of exponential growth in new store openings were over but that the company still maintained a growth ethic.
"At the moment we are really trying to get the thing tuned so that we can take advantage of other types of opportunities," he said, adding the company was well over last year's difficulties.

"Whether they be offshore expansion or moving into other types or franchises or going to supercentres. There are lots of opportunities but we are not even going to think about that until we've got everything very fine-tuned and buttoned down."
In terms of new store growth, Tindall said it would probably settle down to five percent a year in square footage, eventually falling to two percent.
"But as you can see with (offshoot) Warehouse Stationery, there is substantial growth there for us and that sort of begs the question as to what other opportunities are there," he said.
"The company is in a mindset of growth. We are not really looking to fine-tune like a Hallensteins and then hold. The excitement for us is growing."

Comparing the six months to January 1997 to the six months to January 1996, group sales rose 15.2 percent to NZ$361.1 million. Operating earnings rose 50.6 percent to NZ$40.6 million, the pre-tax profit rose 58.3 percent to $36.2 million and tax paid profit rose 55.7 percent to $25.3 million.

Total net debt was NZ$81 million, down from $113 million a year earlier. Undrawn facilities at January 31 totalled $87 million and the net debt to equity ratio improved to 57.7 percent from 83.6 percent.
Same store sales were up 3.8 percent, or NZ$9.0 million, and $35 million of sales came from new stores.
Retail area increased to 2.03 million square feet from 1.81, or 12 percent, and growth in square footage would be around seven percent in the current year, he said.
In the current half to July, there would be no new locations, no replacement stores but eight refurbishments.
In Warehouse Stationery, two stores opened in the six months, bringing the total to 12. Four more will be added before Christmas.
Operating margins for the Warehouse group rose to 11.2 percent from 8.9 percent as a result of the strong trading performance.
"We've held our gross margin and we've reduced the cost of doing business. This was done through information systems working efficiently as opposed to last year," Tindall said.
The Warehouse had also held its labour costs and reduced its advertising costs.
Inventory on hand fell by NZ$9.6 million or 8.1 percent.
Again, Tindall said the focus would be on continuing to fine-tune inventory and on turning over stock much faster.
To achieve that, the company is putting a heavy emphasis on its stock replenishment system and on merchandise planning.
Analysts have forecast a wide range for the full year profit of NZ$33-38 million, which Tindall said reflected the varying perceptions about the company.

"Some think this can't continue and others think this is only the beginning. All we are doing is signalling very clearly, don't go getting it wrong." The Warehouse had previously warned that the second half will not be as good as the first.

Tindall said there would be changes in top management, with him relinquishing his logistics role. Information technology would have a separate focus and property and operations would be split. Current finance director John Vickers would to the property team and a new director would be appointed.
-- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
